caption:
You paste a client's numbers into the same chat you used for someone else's pitch. Nothing bad happens. Then a proposal comes back with the wrong industry in it.

Fix is boring. One ChatGPT project per paying client. Files, chats and instructions live in it, and the memory setting stays project-only so context doesn't wander between accounts. That setting used to be locked at creation — you can now change it in Project settings after the fact.

The standing brief on slide 4 is the part that saves the time. Scope, out of scope, who you're writing for, how they talk. Write it once when you sign, never re-brief again.

One honest caveat: project-only memory is organisation, not confidentiality. If the contract says no third-party processing, that clause still wins.

Save this and set one up for your biggest client. How many clients are currently sharing one chat window?

slides.sub: One ChatGPT project per client. Memory kept inside it.

body.t: A ChatGPT project holds files, chats and instructions in one place. Make one per paying client.
Name it the way your invoices do.
Open the project, three-dot menu, Project settings, Memory.
You can now change this after the project exists.

slides.headline: Paste the standing brief once.
slides.sub: Project instructions. Written once, used in every chat inside it.
slides.label: COPY THIS PROMPT
slides.code:
You are working only on ACME's account.
Facts: B2B logistics, 40 staff, UK.
Contact: Dana, ops director, hates jargon.
Scope: 12-page website copy, fixed fee.
Out of scope: SEO, ads, ongoing edits.
Tone: plain English, short sentences.
Never mention other clients or their work.
If a fact is missing, ask before assuming.

body.t: Project-only memory stops context bleeding between clients.
It is not a confidentiality guarantee.
If a contract bars third-party processing, the setting doesn't change that.
